1. The animation shows a grid of many houses. Each house stands for one historical scenario of buying versus renting. A lit (orange) house means the buyer came out ahead after ten years. A dark house means the renter came out ahead. The caption says the data come from FHFA home prices, BLS rents and Freddie Mac mortgage rates. It is labeled "ILLUSTRATIVE", "US only" and "history, not a forecast."

2. In frame 1 every house is dark. Starting in frame 3, houses light up in orange, beginning at the front-left corner. By frames 4 to 6 most of the grid is lit, and only a strip of dark houses remains at the far right and back.

3. In most of the historical cases shown, buying beat renting over a ten-year hold. In a minority of cases, renting came out ahead. The picture doesn't say how large the gap was in either direction. It also doesn't say what share of houses are lit, or how the costs were counted, such as interest, tax, insurance and repairs.

4. The animation gives no explicit advice. A viewer might loosely take away that buying has more often paid off over ten years in US history, but that it isn't guaranteed. The "history, not a forecast" caption works against treating it as a prediction.

5. The advice in 4 is my own reading. The animation has no on-screen instruction. Its only text is the legend, the data sources, and the caveats that it is illustrative, US-only and not a forecast.
